lead: The idea holds on all three islands. In the morning shade covers 15% to 30% of the street, and most walkers on Malé (56%) and Hulhumalé (82%) are in the sun. By evening 87% to 100% walk in shade. The streets did not change, so distance cannot explain it.

measures.name: Shade coverage of the street
measures.note: morning to evening; Hulhumalé’s 75% is the midpoint of 70 to 80%

measures.name: Pedestrians in shade
measures.note: share of those counted, morning to evening

notes: Shade grows from 15% to 85%; pedestrians in shade rise too, but evening activity is only 1.3 times higher.
Shade reaches 100% by evening and almost all pedestrians are in it. Evening activity doubles, on small counts: 14 and 28 people.
Shade rises to 70–80%; pedestrians in shade rise sharply, and evening activity reaches 3.6 times the morning level.

caption.label: Figure
caption.text: Outlined bar: morning. Solid bar: evening.

conclusion: Shade grows from morning to evening, and as it does more pedestrians walk in it and street activity rises.
